code: OSS-Fuzz report identifies php-fuzz-mbstring heap-use-after-free in check_called_node_in_look_behind / check_node_in_look_behind
note: The vulnerable target is PHP mbstring regex handling; the crash is triggered by attacker-controlled multibyte input reaching the mbstring conversion path.
This regression test shows the exact attacker-controlled byte sequence that exercises the CP950 decoder.

code: case 0: if (c > c1 && c < 0xff) { filter->status = 1; filter->cache = c; }
note: The first byte 0x81 is treated as a DBCS lead byte and cached for the next call.
The second byte 0x3a is accepted as a valid trail byte, so the decoder computes a Big5 index and then falls through the CP950 PUA handling path.
Before the fix, the CP950 PUA condition was overly broad and could mis-handle invalid lead/trail combinations, leading to out-of-bounds table access in the conversion logic.
